title: Splitting factors of a finite indexed product of prime elements
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative integral domain, that is, a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors. For $q,y\in D$ write $q\mid y$ when $y$ lies in the $D$-submodule $\operatorname{span}_D\{q\}=qD$ of $D$ spanned by $q$ [def-weil-submodule-span], i.e. $y=qz$ for some $z\in D$. Let $I$ be a set, $S\subset I$ a finite subset, and $p:I\to D$ a family such that for every $i\in S$ the element $p_i$ is prime: $p_i\ne0$, $p_i$ is not a unit, and $p_i\mid ab$ implies $p_i\mid a$ or $p_i\mid b$ for all $a,b\in D$. Let $h,k,a\in D$ satisfy $hk=a\prod_{i\in S}p_i$. Then there are finite subsets $T,U\subset I$ and elements $b,c\in D$ such that $T\cup U=S$, $T\cap U=\varnothing$, $a=bc$, $h=b\prod_{i\in T}p_i$, and $k=c\prod_{i\in U}p_i$. The empty subset and repeated or associated values of $p$ are allowed; unique factorization of $D$ is not assumed.
